- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often overcorrects downward — adjust upward to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- Model frequently underestimates sharp upward moves (especially after sentiment spikes) — add a small lagged momentum buffer to forecast.  
- Model overestimates downward moves after recent highs — apply mean reversion bias toward prior 5-7 day average if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underpredicts late-period price surges — increase forecast by 1-2% for days 25-30 if sentiment is rising.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.33), model tends to smooth too much — allow 1-2% asymmetric adjustment toward recent sentiment direction.
